newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Zao Svift wins tender for 38 pct of Norilsk Nickel.
newsitem.headline: Zao Svift wins tender for 38 pct of Norilsk Nickel.

text.p: Russian firm ZAO Svift has won a tender for a 38 percent stake in the Norilsk Nickel metals group with a bid of 236.18 million European currency units ($250.1 million), an official said on Tuesday.

Dmitry Ushakov, chairman of the tender committee and a deputy chairman of commercial bank Uneximbank, the vendor of the stake, also said that the only other bidder was Peredovye Promyshlennye Tekhnologii (Advanced Industrial Technologies), an unknown Russian firm.
An Uneximbank source who did not wish to be identified said Svift represented Uneximbank's interests.
"The Svift bid is higher than that of Advanced Industrial Technologies, and we therefore name the shareholding company Svift the winner of the contest," Ushakov told reporters.

He said there were no foreign participants in the Russian companies which placed bids and that the losing bidder offered 171.0 million ECUs for the Norilsk stake, which represents 51 percent of voting shares. The starting price for the stake was 131.6 million ECUs. In addition, the winner is required to invest at least $300 million in Norilsk, pay off some of its debts and assume certain costs.

The sale of Norilsk, one of Russia's leading industrial enterprises and a major international producer of base and precious metals, took place despite Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's order on Monday that it be suspended.

Uneximbank, one of Russia's leading commercial banks, has been under fire from major media and banking officials since it won a tender for a quarter stake in the Svyazinvest telecoms holding earlier this month.
Uneximbank had been widely expected to retain control of the 38 percent Norilsk stake.
